purpose: Measure reproducibility BEFORE freezing any tolerance, per the audit's sequencing.

FINDING.within_environment: BIT-IDENTICAL. Two independent runs of the rebuilt stage on this machine agree exactly on every family margin and LCB.
FINDING.cross_environment: The committed frozen artifact differs by at most 1.041e-16 absolute.
FINDING.CORRECTION_TO_MY_EARLIER_HYPOTHESIS: I suggested the frozen artifact might simply not be bit-reproducible, i.e. that the computation was nondeterministic. The repeat run refutes that: it IS bit-reproducible within an environment. The residual is ENVIRONMENT-DEPENDENT (numpy/BLAS build, threading, or machine), which is a different and more precise statement.
FINDING.why_this_matters: A tolerance is justified not because the computation is random - it is not - but because the frozen reference was produced in a different numerical environment. That distinction changes what the tolerance is FOR.

DECISION_IMPACT.statement: The largest observed deviation is roughly fourteen orders of magnitude below the smallest distance between any family's LCB and the M_MIN=0.010 decision threshold. It cannot flip a PASS/FAIL.

PROPOSED_FROZEN_TOLERANCE.applies_to: absolute agreement of family margins and LCB95 against the committed frozen reference
justification_order: tolerance set ~4 orders of magnitude above the measured deviation and ~10 orders below the smallest decision gap
PROPOSED_FROZEN_TOLERANCE.explicitly_not: a tolerance chosen to make a near-miss pass; the measurement preceded the number
